claims.text: Argon–nitrogen annealing combined with cyclic longitudinal tensile straining induces favorable nanograin geometry.
The combined treatment produces controlled defect structures.
The treatment-induced grain geometry and defects align magnetic domains.
The treatment-induced grain geometry and defects minimize magnetic-domain pinning.
The proposed structural tuning enhances the magnetocaloric response at low applied fields.
Optimized nanograin geometry and strain-induced defects improve magnetic exchange.
Optimized nanograin geometry and strain-induced defects preserve continuous thermal-conduction pathways.
An argon–nitrogen annealing atmosphere facilitates controlled grain growth.
An argon–nitrogen annealing atmosphere passivates defects.
Cyclic tensile straining introduces beneficial strain fields.
The combined microstructural changes enhance magnetic-domain alignment under low applied fields.
The combined microstructural changes reduce energy barriers for magnetization reversal.
Reduced barriers to magnetization reversal lower magnetic hysteresis.
Interconnected microstructures enable rapid heat exchange.
Interconnected microstructures maintain mechanical rigidity.
Relative to pure-argon annealing without cyclic straining, the combined treatment will produce a larger low-field magnetocaloric entropy or temperature change.
Relative to the baseline, the combined treatment will reduce hysteresis during magnetic cycling.
Relative to the baseline, the combined treatment will maintain or improve thermal conductivity.
Relative to the baseline, the combined treatment will maintain or improve mechanical stability.

The proposed effects are expected to hold for rare-earth-free high-entropy-alloy thin films and nanoribbons processed under comparable thermal and atmospheric conditions, while applicability to bulk materials or other alloy systems is uncertain.
